# E02 T1 implementation report

All 23 commands in docs/build/E02/T1.gates pass through `sh scripts/gates.sh docs/build/E02/T1.gates` (exit 0) on
the branch merged with main (2c56774), in this worktree and again in a fresh clone of that merge commit. The E02 suite
has 118 hub and eval tests, 25 Vitest tests and 7 Playwright tests, with no skips, xfails, deselections or silenced
checks. Branch coverage of E02 domain and application code is 96.53 percent. The whole hub suite passes (1159 tests,
main's modules included).

E02 is built as far as its seams allow today. Sign-in, sessions, roster, credentials, adapter tokens, the attempt
limits, consent grants with their time fences, the record authorization binding, the owner and operator consoles
and the crew app session lock are complete and tested against real SQLite, real Argon2id, the real E01 composition
root and a real browser. Four design test IDs (T-E02-002, 005, 017, 021) and parts of six others depend on epics or
requests that do not exist yet; they are listed under Limitations with the interim that keeps each one closed.

## Built

Hub, identity (hub/src/crew_health/identity/)

- domain/session.py: principal kinds, roles from kind and officer rank only, session facts and liveness, lifetimes
  capped at `security.idle_lock_minutes` for people, oldest-first replacement past `identity.sessions_per_principal`.
- domain/limits.py: principal, client and global attempt buckets with windowed debt, refund and reclaim.
- domain/roster.py: whole-document roster validation, member and principal ceilings, display names kept exactly.
- domain/routing.py: subject binding for manual capture (E02 3.4): self capture, or the acting medical officer
  entering for a named roster member; officer status grants no chart read.
- application/service.py: sign-in as a reservation unit of work, one bounded Argon2id verification outside the
  writer, then an issuance unit of work that rechecks principal, generation, verifier and roster; per-request
  authentication; sign-out with the S5.8 ledger; restart and removal ending sessions; the listCrew page.
- application/admin.py: roster bootstrap and change, first credential provisioning by an operator, owner credential
  change proven under the sign-in limits, adapter tokens issued once by an operator.
- application/settings.py, support.py, store.py, ports.py: the E02 11 settings with their bounds, audit
  declarations, the store protocol and the ports other modules consume (IdentityPorts, SessionReader, HubProfile).
- adapters/repository.py with migrations/0001_identity.sql, adapters/credentials.py (Argon2id at the design's fixed
  parameters, tokens stored only as digests), adapters/vault.py (`PrivateKeyVault` location, unavailable).
- api/router.py: `createSession`, `getCurrentSession`, `deleteCurrentSession`, `listCrew` and the security
  dependency E01's app uses for every operation's roles.
- cli.py and schemas/roster-bootstrap.schema.json: the operator console (roster, credentials, adapter tokens).
- module.py: registration with E01's registry (settings, ID prefixes, audience rule, ports, router) and the
  startup sweep that ends every session of an earlier process.

Hub, consent (hub/src/crew_health/consent/)

- domain/grants.py: owner-only, prospective, exact grants (recipient, mission, origin, object, purpose, actions,
  fields, validity); `grants_now` denies any unknown or terminal fact, and a finite grant also needs its issuing
  process epoch and an elapsed monotonic time below its span.
- application/service.py: `allows` and `fields` queries over the caller's snapshot, grant and revoke in the
  caller's unit of work with reference-only audit, absolute expiry scheduled through S5.10, fences on clock
  correction, clock regression and restart, and the owner listing.
- application/records.py: the record authorization E01's records module calls (owner, explicit grant, officer
  capture for a member, the author's read-back of its own record).
- adapters/repository.py with migrations/0001_consent.sql, cli.py (owner console), module.py.

Crew app (ui/crew/)

- src/features/identity/sessionLock.ts (E02): the lock, its deadline from the session's own life counted from
  sign-in dispatch on both clocks, the wipe, station and hub order, browser lifecycle binding and the station screen.
- The minimal E03 shell that hosts it, listed under E03-owned files created.

Tests and tools

- hub/tests/identity, hub/tests/consent, hub/tests/privacy (with the shared SIM station in
  hub/tests/privacy/e02_station.py, which also serves the browser tests), eval/scenarios/E02/test_privacy_acceptance.py,
  ui/crew/src/features/identity/sessionLock.test.ts and sessionLock.spec.ts.

Reused from E01, unchanged: kernel errors, unit of work, identifiers, clock, command ledger, storage, settings,
scheduler, private and audit protocols; platform storage, audit policies and the SQLite test database; the app
registry, assembly and `create_app`; PersistentClocks; the config release loader; the events delivery; records;
contracts_gen schemas and enums. From the TypeScript package: `@crew-health/contracts` (`client`, `components`).

Shared files changed: hub/pyproject.toml (argon2-cffi, package data for the two migrations and the roster schema),
hub/uv.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml (ui/crew importer), hub/src/crew_health/contracts_gen/manifest.json (D26) and its

The storage failure matrix (hub/tests/privacy/test_faults.py) runs sign-in, sign-out, credential change, roster
change, adapter token issue, grant and revoke through a unit of work factory that fails step N with
`StorageUnavailable("disk_full")`, for every N, both before the step and after it has written. Each test asserts the
phases it reached (statements, audit, replication reference, schedule or cancel, commit). A deliberately swallowed
audit failure in revoke made it fail, so the matrix detects a swallowed storage error.

gates passed there with exit 0 and the same counts; afterwards `git status` showed no tracked change. Windows and
Linux were not run natively. Gate 4 proves every runtime and dev dependency installs from wheels on Windows, and the
crew app's scripts and configuration run no shell commands.

Not gates, and why: `scripts/validate_hub.py corpus safety trace` fail on E01-owned state (complexity in
platform/private.py, missing T-E01-10 and T-E01-19 markers, contributors not built yet) and do not cover E02 yet
(R-E02-22). `scripts/validate_contracts.py` reports 305 problems that predate this branch in docs/product. All four
give the same result after the merge.

## Merge with main

Commit 2c56774 merges origin/main at dd644bc (28 commits) with no textual conflict. Main added the trends, groundlink
and catchup hub modules, changed help, and added workers/forecast, three configuration documents
(config/environment-hazards.json, config/environment-profiles.json, config/ui-copy.json), NASA data and package
updates. It changed no E02 file and nothing under ui/, and left pnpm-lock.yaml, hub/pyproject.toml and hub/uv.lock
untouched.

Both sides had changed the generated manifests hub/src/crew_health/contracts_gen/manifest.json and
packages/contracts-ts/src/generated/manifest.json. After the merge both were regenerated with their generators
(gates 1 and 2): the output matched the merged files byte for byte and holds the identity, consent, catchup,
groundlink and trends module hashes. `uv lock --check --project hub` passes.

What the merge changed for E02:

- The whole hub suite grew from 816 to 1159 tests and the generated import contracts from 157 to 241; all pass. E02's
  own counts and coverage are unchanged.
- Main's config/ui-copy.json has no `shell_words` (no station title, sign-in, sign-out or PIN label), so X-E03-1's
  interim holds and the station screen keeps its empty heading. Its `error_messages.UNAUTHENTICATED` could word the
  station screen after a 401 lock once E03's copy loader (`copy.ts`) and the pre-session bootstrap (X-E03-19) exist.
- Main's AGENTS.md section 1 rule 9 asks for each file built in another epic's paths to be listed;
  docs/build/E03/BUILT-BY-OTHERS.md lists the 16 crew app shell files. Main has no files under ui/crew, so no shell
  had to be merged.

## Real and faked

Real in every hub test: SQLite through E01's `SQLiteDatabase` with its authorizer, audit chain, command ledger,
scheduler and replication references; Argon2id at 64 MiB, 3 iterations, parallelism 4; E02 migrations applied by
the composer. Real in the HTTP and acceptance tests: E01's `create_app`, middleware, generated models, config release
activation, PersistentClocks and event delivery. Real in Playwright: the hub serving over uvicorn
(hub/tests/privacy/e02_station.py `main`), Vite's dev server and Chromium.

Faked or substituted:

- Time is `MemoryClock` from kernel.testing (SIM clock at 2026-11-14T08:00Z); PersistentClocks runs over it.
- Data is the SIM roster built from the package examples (docs/product/api/examples), loaded only by the test
  station.
- Configuration release checks for contributors that do not exist yet are `MemoryReleaseCheck` passes.
- The private vault is `UnavailableVault`: it refuses every allocation and unwrap (R-E02-20).
- E01's records module gets a synthetic quality policy in the test station only.
- Playwright cannot sign in through the app because the sign-in words do not exist (X-E03-1), so each spec composes
  the production modules (session store, API client, lock) inside the page as main.ts does, with a recording station
  screen and a skewable clock, and signs in through the real `createSession`.
- Headless Chromium never fires `visibilitychange`, `freeze` or `resume`, and Vite's dev socket blocks the
  back-forward cache, so hiding, suspension and bfcache restore are proven in jsdom; Playwright proves the pagehide
  lock and that Back shows no private content either way.

## Design corrections

1. Author read-back. E01's records assembly reads a created record back through `require_read`; with owner and
   grant rules alone, an officer's committed capture for a member answered 403 after it was stored. Consent
   admits the session that authored that one record (`AuthoredRecords`), nothing more. Evidence:
   test_record_authorization_needs_the_composer_bound_authored_records and
   test_self_capture_and_officer_capture_for_a_roster_member. Request R-E02-25.
2. `AuthoredRecords` is bound by the composer: the import contracts forbid consent importing records.
3. Console bootstrap trust. The physical console is trusted for the first roster document only; once an operator
   principal exists, every console command needs the operator credential on standard input, and a console with no
   operator on the roster refuses everything (test_first_bootstrap_then_every_console_command_needs_the_operator_credential,
   test_a_console_without_an_operator_on_the_roster_refuses_every_command).
4. Console commands are guarded by expected revisions and credential generations, not S5.8 command identity (design
   section 4, roster row). A retried command fails STALE_VERSION and can never apply twice; a console run retried
   by hand is a new process with no stable command key.
5. Finite grants are built with the fence R-E02-21 proposes, not kept off as its interim says: absolute expiry
   scheduled in the grant's unit of work, `grants_now` denying at `valid_until` and on a changed process epoch or an
   elapsed monotonic time past the span, and every finite grant fenced inside the clock's own correction or
   regression transaction and at startup. Evidence: hub/tests/consent/test_consent_time.py with the real
   PersistentClocks, and test_time_ends_finite_grants_and_neither_correction_nor_restart_revives_them. The
   coordinator (Joaquin Castellano) accepted it as built; docs/requests/E02.md records R-E02-21 as answered.
6. Adapter tokens are `identity_session` rows of kind adapter, not a separate `identity_adapter_token` table (design
   section 5): same digest, expiry, listener, generation and revocation, one authentication path.
7. Roster removal is final: `removed_at` is set, the credential disabled, sessions end, and re-adding the person is
   INVALID_TRANSITION.
8. Ground sign-in exists only when the composer provides `HubProfile` for a ground or demo hub; absent, ground is
   refused like a wrong secret.
9. A `deleteCurrentSession` retried with an ended token answers 401, as the design's sign-out row says, not an S5.8
   replay: authentication runs before the ledger.
10. `SessionReader.alive` was added so E01's event delivery can revalidate an open stream at each heartbeat
    (test_an_open_event_stream_ends_at_its_next_heartbeat_once_the_member_is_removed).
11. A credential change is proven through the sign-in path and its limits, so guessing through the console costs the
    same attempts as guessing at sign-in.
12. The crew app checks its deadline on the monotonic and the wall clock and the earlier wins: `performance.now` can
    pause while a laptop sleeps, and a wall clock correction must never extend a session.
13. The crew app asks the hub to end the session on every lock except a 401, where the hub has already ended it.
14. The owner listing returns every active grant (at most the 256 ceiling) and one page of the newest ended grants
    with an `older` flag; the console prints `{"older_ended_grants": true}` after the page. It replaces one query
    limited to four times the active ceiling, which truncated history silently and, at the setting's maximum, asked
    storage for more rows than `storage.max_rows` allows
    (test_the_owner_list_holds_every_active_grant_and_says_when_older_ended_ones_are_left_out).
15. Identity and consent refuse to start with CONFIG_INVALID when `storage.max_rows` is 256 or less, because a
    complete read of the roster or of one subject's active grants needs 257 rows
    (test_identity_refuses_to_start_when_storage_cannot_return_a_whole_roster,
    test_consent_refuses_to_start_when_storage_cannot_return_every_active_grant).
16. A roster change reads every current member and checks re-adds by exact person IDs. It replaced a page over the
    whole person history that, after enough removals, hid a current member from removal
    (test_a_long_roster_history_never_hides_a_current_member_from_removal fails on the earlier code: p19 stayed on
    the roster).

## Requirements over looks

- The station screen has an empty heading and no title, sign-in or sign-out controls: no words exist in
  configuration yet (X-E03-1), and rule 1 forbids literal UI copy.
- Fonts fall back to system fonts; the design system's faces are not vendored (R-E02-28).
- ProfileView shows only the display name the hub returned, the least private content that proves the lock.
- Roster, credential and consent management are console commands with JSON lines, not screens, until R-E02-1 and
  the words exist.

## Limitations

- T-E02-002 (help summary): no E26 help membership fact exists; summary projection stays off (R-E02-10).
- T-E02-005 (demo presenter): no explicit demo profile or presenter mapping is built; a person without a roster
  entry cannot sign in, so presenter routing and capture fail closed (E21, R-E02-9).
- T-E02-017 (report sharing): off until R-E02-19 and its E09, E16 and E29 providers exist.
- T-E02-021 (configuration): only its settings clause is tested (settings changed at restart neither extend a
  session nor revive a grant). The ui-copy label and release activation clauses wait for words (X-E03-1) and E20.
- T-E02-006 and T-E02-014 are partial: sign-in failures never echo the secret and no token or credential is stored
  in plain text, but there is no journal, so no canary, and the vault is `UnavailableVault` with no crash matrix on
  a real backend (R-E02-20).
- T-E02-008 covers a removed member's open stream ending at its next heartbeat; a console revoke with an open stream
  and buffered events waits for consent projections on streams (R-E02-11).
- T-E02-011 does not cover the original owner's encrypted offline queue or P2 and P3 drafts: E03 has no queue or
  drafts yet.
- T-E02-012 models a crash as a storage failure before commit at every step; SQLite's own atomicity across a real
  process kill is E01's platform test.
- T-E02-016 covers a saturated verifier failing fast; the fixed emergency cache and printed fallback are E26 and E03.
- No mutation run: the repository has no mutation tool yet (R-E02-22).
- AI-USE-LOG.md has no row for this build: the file is outside this task's paths; the coordinator adds it.
